summary.headline: Enviro Infra FY26 revenue rose 7.5% to INR11,456 mn, missing 35% guidance; FY27 guided to ~INR2,000 crore revenue with 13.5-14% PAT margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR4,273 mn (+8.8% YoY), EBITDA INR799 mn (18.7% margin) and PAT INR543 mn (12.4% margin), with margin pressure attributed to renewable IPP mix, higher employee cost, ECL provision and depreciation. Management said FY26 revenue partly missed guidance because awarded projects stayed in design and bid evaluations were delayed, and it cut FY27 EBITDA guidance to 21-22% from 22-24% citing commodity cost pressure. Working capital stretched to 166 days (unbilled revenue days at 195) because AMRUT state-scheme funds were delayed. The renewable segment (BESS, wind EPC via Suyog Urja) is now a major part of the order book.

financial_highlights.value: INR422 crore (LT INR250 crore, ST INR175 crore)

segments.name: Water & wastewater
segments.commentary: Execution order book about INR2,733 crore plus O&M order book about INR951 crore; FY27 water/wastewater revenue expected about INR1,350 crore. Recent wins: INR348 crore BUIDCO (Bihar) project and two Swachh Bharat sanitation projects in Pune and Nashik worth INR824 crore in Q4.

segments.name: Renewable energy
segments.commentary: Execution order book about INR2,051 crore plus O&M/IPP about INR1,079 crore; renewable revenue was about INR129 crore in FY26 (INR117 crore in Q4, mostly IPP with near-zero margin). FY27 renewable revenue target about INR650 crore; BESS EPC PAT margin guided about 10%, renewables blended PAT 10-12%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about INR2,000 crore, with PAT of INR270-280 crore (13.5-14% PAT margin).
FY27 EBITDA margin cut to 21-22% from earlier 22-24%, with a possible further 1-2 percentage point dip from commodity and geopolitical cost pressure.
FY27 order inflow target of at least INR2,500 crore; bid pipeline submitted about INR1,200 crore plus about INR5,000 crore under evaluation.
Working capital cycle targeted to fall to about 90 days; debt-to-equity to be capped at 1:1 on consolidated basis.
Capex for FY27 expected at about INR20-30 crore; Q1 FY27 revenue said to be well above Q1 FY26 (about INR250 crore), without a number.
FY28 indicative revenue from existing order book about INR2,500-2,800 crore; management reiterated 35-40% long-term topline growth ambition.
capex_capacity: Total execution order book about INR4,800 crore, said to give visibility over FY27 and FY28 (execution period 18-24 months for renewable projects).
BESS: 4 NTPC EPC projects totalling 930 MWh worth about INR1,070 crore (UP, Assam, Karnataka, Telangana) plus acquired 150 MWh Bihar BESS project.
Lithium-ion cell procurement deferred due to price rises; BOS works (civil, transformers, HT lines) already started.
Renewable team above 250 professionals; business heads appointed for each division.
Asset monetisation possible if leverage rises; Suyog Urja (wind EPC) acquired during FY26.
demand_pricing: Most contracts carry a price variation clause, which offsets only part of the cost increase; management says guidance was lowered for this gap.
Water project cost benchmarks: STP INR1-1.5 crore per MLD; water treatment INR30-50 lakh per MLD; CETP highly variable (INR2-15 crore per MLD).
Design component is 2-5% of turnkey water project value; STPs and CETPs are the most technology-intensive.

Revenue shortfall attributed to slow evaluations and re-bidding of an MIDC CETP/ZLD project and two Bangalore projects stuck in design, plus delayed AMRUT funds in Chhattisgarh, MP, Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab.
Renewable receivables de-risked via NTPC and A-to-AAA rated private clients for Suyog's wind EPC work.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 revenue guidance (about 35% growth) missed and is execution delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ongoing projects have no delays, but the order book of about INR1,200 crore at 1 April 2025 converted to about INR1,145 crore (about 95%) with timing slipping; some projects stayed in design and a re-bid hit timelines. Renewables were about INR100 crore below the INR200 crore guidance and wastewater about INR100 crore below as well.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins fall and what is the underlying margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited mix: about INR100-120 crore of zero-margin IPP revenue, employee cost up to about 6% of revenue, other expenses 3.5%, ECL provision INR10 crore and depreciation up about INR25 crore. Manufacturing cost fell about 1 percentage point; FY26 EBITDA stayed above 24%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of renewable revenue in FY26 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewable revenue was about INR129 crore for FY26, with about INR12 crore up to December and INR117 crore in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook and drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital cycle was 166 days, with UBR days at 195 because AMRUT funds were not released; receivable days fell to 53. Management expects funds from Chhattisgarh and a path for Rajasthan, Haryana and MP, targeting about 90 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 EBITDA guidance be cut further and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cut EBITDA guidance to 21-22% from 22-24% due to commodity and geopolitical cost pressure; a further 1-2 point dip is possible, depending on whether the situation stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BESS and renewable margins and how is the FY27 revenue split?
qa_highlights.answer: BESS EPC PAT margin is about 10%; renewable blended PAT target is 10-12%. FY27 revenue split is about INR1,350 crore water/wastewater and INR650 crore renewables, against the INR2,000 crore total; about 42% of the INR4,800 crore order book.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating cash flow position?
qa_highlights.answer: Adjusted pre-tax OCF is roughly balanced (about INR4 lakh positive) in FY26; post-tax OCF is negative INR63 crore, mainly due to service concession receivables recognised in OCF under audit policy.

risks_watch: Delayed central and state fund release (AMRUT, Jal Jeevan) could keep UBR days near 195 and working capital above 166 days.
Lithium-ion cell cost increases and geopolitical commodity pressure could cut EBITDA by a further 1-2 percentage points.
Revenue execution slippage: FY26 missed guidance; FY27 guidance of about INR2,000 crore depends on converting only about 42% of the INR4,800 crore order book.
Renewable IPP projects carry near-zero margin; segment profitability disclosure is promised separately going forward.
Debt rising toward the stated 1:1 debt-to-equity ceiling as renewable development projects are funded.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book visibility and FY27 targets, but defensive on the FY26 miss and margin compression; management repeatedly described guidance as deliberately conservative and admitted the revenue guidance was not met.
key_quotes: So we are just projecting a topline of INR2,000-odd crores, which will replicate into a conversion of somewhere around 42%. So we are trying ourselves to be just too conservative this time so that there is no fallback at all.
We will delay the procurement of lithium-ion battery to a certain extent so the prices get settled down, and at that point of time, we'll go for the procurement.
So as such, I can confirm with respect to the execution, the delay was not there.

adds.what: 4 NTPC BESS EPC projects totalling 930 MWh (UP, Assam, Karnataka, Telangana) plus acquired 150 MWh Bihar BESS project

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to about INR2,000 crore versus FY26 INR1,146 crore (~17.5% growth), backed by a INR4,800 crore execution order book and BESS EPC projects, though the brief gives no timing for the BESS capacity and EBITDA margin guidance was cut to 21-22%.
